basis: Defining mitochondrial defect, cardiomyopathy and psychomotor delay; hepatic injury in 4/5. Single reported renal lesion omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: psychomotor delay is a defining manifestation; global developmental delay is documented in 1/1 annotated patient.

basis: Fibrous dysplasia, pigmentary lesions and endocrine hyperfunction define MAS. Phosphate wasting reflects FGF23 action rather than intrinsic kidney damage.

decisions.renal: none: the 30-79% tubular dysfunction annotation largely reflects FGF23-mediated phosphate wasting; it does not establish direct renal injury.

basis: Collagen VI muscular dystrophy damages skeletal muscle and causes contractures; ventilatory failure results from respiratory muscle weakness.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure (1/1 annotated) is neuromuscular; common ventilatory insufficiency does not establish direct lung or airway damage.

basis: Tentative craniocardioskeletal identification; cutis laxa is characteristic in the original four cases. [Report](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7151302/)

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac malformations define the tentatively identified craniocardioskeletal syndrome; exact eponym mapping remains uncertain.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is characteristic of the tentatively identified craniocardioskeletal syndrome.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: characteristic cutis laxa in the original four-case description; this assignment does not assume classic Cantu hypertrichosis.

basis: Skeletal dystrophy and frequently associated cardiomyopathy are explicit defining features; respiratory muscle impairment does not establish pulmonary damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy is explicitly included in the disease definition and supported by its familial dilated cardiomyopathy parent.

basis: Blood/marrow T-cell leukemia; hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly 40-50%. Skin infiltration is generally below 30%.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: this concept is a leukemia, not an infection, immunodeficiency, autoimmune disease or lymphoma; lymphoid lineage alone does not qualify.

basis: Platelet dysfunction and oculocutaneous albinism define HPS; pulmonary fibrosis 30-79% by HPO. Renal insufficiency omitted at cap; immunodeficiency is subtype-specific.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent skin/hair hypopigmentation is part of defining oculocutaneous albinism, present in most patients.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: inferred from organelle-trafficking pathogenesis rather than a defined metabolic defect. [GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1287/)

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment, persistent HbF (4/5) and defining lymphoid hyperplasia localized to adenoids (12/12). Recurrent URIs do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: named lymphoid hyperplasia is localized to nasopharyngeal adenoids in 12/12; nasopharyngeal airway tissue falls within pulmonary.

basis: TBX21 immunodeficiency with intrinsic Th2-associated persistent airway inflammation in the sole reported patient (1/1); population frequency remains uncertain.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: persistent reactive airway inflammation is an intrinsic Th2 immune-dysregulation manifestation in 1/1 patient, rather than infection risk alone.

basis: Inherited functional fibrinogen disorder. Despite HPO thrombosis frequency of 30-79%, thrombotic events are separately diagnosed complications; bleeding sites do not imply local disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: HPO reports venous thrombosis in 30-79%, but these are separately diagnosed thrombotic events whose risk is raised by the coagulation disorder.
